what: `#[rustc_builtin_macro(blaze_unreachable)] pub macro unreachable() {}` in core::blaze was taken for the builtin `unreachable` (the macro`s own name): the explicit name in the attribute was read for `macro_rules!` only. The lint that looks for the builtin found 0 sites and its accepting test passed with nothing checked.
cost: 15 minutes; found only because the refusing test expected 5 findings and got 0
cause: two copies of `which builtin is this macro` (one per macro kind), and only one read the attribute`s argument
whys: the call resolved to the builtin `unreachable`, not `blaze_unreachable`
Macro2 collection looked the builtin up by the item`s name only
the rule lives twice, once per macro kind, and the copies drifted
a test that expects no findings passes when the check runs on nothing
class: a rule written once per item kind drifts; and an accept-only test cannot tell `proved` from `not looked at`
prevention: fixed for this case: Macro2 reads the explicit name too (this lane). Not built: one function both kinds call. Each accepting test in reach_tests.rs has a refusing twin over the same macro, so a check that finds no site fails a test.
fix: merge the two `Case 1: builtin macros` blocks of collect.rs into one function
